Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 63, verses 1–6:

It is Madani.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1} When the Prophet (ﷺ) arrived in Madinah, Islam spread there and grew strong, and some people among its inhabitants from the Aws and the Khazraj began to show faith while concealing disbelief, so that their standing would remain, their blood would be protected, and their wealth would be safe. Allah mentioned among their attributes that by which they may be recognized, so that the servants would beware of them and be aware of them. He said: {When the hypocrites come to you, they say}: in a manner of falsehood: {"We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of Allah."} This testimony from the hypocrites is in a manner of falsehood and hypocrisy, even though there is no need for their testimony to confirm His Messenger, for Allah {knows that you are indeed His Messenger, and Allah bears witness that the hypocrites are indeed liars} in their words and their claims, and that this is not a reality from them.

{2} {They have taken their oaths as a shield}; that is, a shield with which they protect themselves from being attributed to hypocrisy. {And they averted [others] from His way}: they averted themselves, and they averted others who were unaware of their condition. {Indeed, evil is what they have been doing}: in that they showed faith, concealed disbelief, swore to that, and gave the impression of their sincerity.

{3} {That} is because of the fact that they, having {believed and then disbelieved}, were not steadfast in faith. Rather, {their hearts were sealed}, so that good never enters them at all. {So they do not understand}: what would benefit them, and they do not comprehend what would return to their interests.

{4} {And when you see them, their bodies please you}: with their fine appearance and freshness. {And if they speak, you listen to their speech}; that is, you find delight in listening to their eloquent speech. Their bodies and their words are pleasing, but beyond that there is nothing of noble character or righteous guidance. Therefore He said: {as if they were propped-up pieces of wood}: having no benefit in them, and nothing is gained from them except pure harm. {They think every cry is against them}: this is due to their cowardice, fear, weakness of heart and their doubt; they fear that their secret will be exposed. Those are {the enemy} in truth, for a visible, distinct enemy is easier than an enemy whose presence is unnoticed, who is deceitful and cunning, claiming to be a friend while being the clear enemy. {So beware of them. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?}; that is, how are they turned away from the Islamic religion after its proofs have become clear and its features evident, toward disbelief, which brings them nothing but loss and misery.

{5} {And when it is said} to these hypocrites: {"Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you"} for what has proceeded from you, so that your condition may improve and your deeds be accepted: they refused this most strongly, and {they turn their heads away}, refusing to seek the supplication of the Messenger. {And you see them turning away} from the truth out of hatred for it, {while they are arrogant} in not following it, out of transgression and obstinacy. This is their state when they are called to seek the supplication of the Messenger.

{6} This is from Allah's kindness and honor toward His Messenger, for they did not come to him so that he might ask forgiveness for them. For {it is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will not forgive them}. That is because they are a people of defiance, outside obedience to Allah, preferring disbelief over faith; therefore the Messenger's seeking forgiveness would not benefit them even if he sought it, as Allah the Exalted said: {"Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them."} {Indeed, Allah does not guide the defiant people.}

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 63, verses 9–11:

{9} Allah, the Exalted, commands His believing servants to remember Him often, for in that lies profit, success, and abundant good. He forbids them to let their wealth and their children distract them from His remembrance, for the love of wealth and children is innate in most souls, so they prefer it over the love of Allah, and in that lies a tremendous loss. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And whoever does that﴾; that is, whoever is diverted by his wealth and his children from the remembrance of Allah, ﴿those are the losers﴾: of eternal happiness and everlasting bliss, because they preferred what perishes over what endures. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial, and with Allah is a great reward.﴾

{10} His saying: ﴿And spend from what We have provided for you﴾ includes obligatory expenditures such as zakat, expiations (kaffarat), the maintenance of wives and slaves, and the like, as well as recommended expenditures, such as spending wealth on all the good causes. He said: ﴿from what We have provided for you﴾, to indicate that Allah, the Exalted, has not burdened His servants with spending that would distress them and be hard upon them. Rather, He commanded them to give out a portion of what He has provided them, and He made it easy for them and eased its means. Let them thank the One who gave them by consoling their needy brethren, and let them hasten to do so before death comes, when a servant cannot bring even an atom's weight of good. For this reason He said: ﴿before death comes to one of you, and he says﴾, lamenting what he neglected while it was still possible, asking for a return, which is impossible: ﴿My Lord, if only You would delay me to a near term﴾; that is, so that I may make up for what I neglected, ﴿and I would give charity﴾: from my wealth, by which I may be saved from punishment and deserve abundant reward, ﴿and be among the righteous﴾: by performing all the commanded duties and avoiding all the forbidden things. This includes Hajj and other acts.

{11} This request and wish has passed its time and cannot be made up, for this reason He said: ﴿And Allah will never delay a soul when its term has come﴾: its predetermined end. ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾: of good and evil, and He will reward you for what He knows of your intentions and deeds.

The commentary on Surah al-Munafiqun is complete. All praise is due to Allah.

The commentary on Surah al-Munafiqun is complete. All praise is due to Allah.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 63, verses 9–11:

{9} Allah, the Exalted, commands His believing servants to remember Him often, for in that lies profit, success, and abundant good. He forbids them to let their wealth and their children distract them from His remembrance, for the love of wealth and children is innate in most souls, so they prefer it over the love of Allah, and in that lies a tremendous loss. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And whoever does that﴾; that is, whoever is diverted by his wealth and his children from the remembrance of Allah, ﴿those are the losers﴾: of eternal happiness and everlasting bliss, because they preferred what perishes over what endures. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial, and with Allah is a great reward.﴾

{10} His saying: ﴿And spend from what We have provided for you﴾ includes obligatory expenditures such as zakat, expiations (kaffarat), the maintenance of wives and slaves, and the like, as well as recommended expenditures, such as spending wealth on all the good causes.
